items.heading: Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation)
details: The sequence of stretches gently warms up nearly every major muscle group in the body.
Practicing outdoors at sunrise combines light exercise with early sunlight, a natural source of vitamin D, and the synchronized breathing is a simple grounding technique.

items.heading: Pranayama
details: Controlled breathing can influence autonomic nervous system activity and promote relaxation.

items.heading: Nadi Shodhana (alternate-nostril breathing)
details: Can promote relaxation and support focused attention through slow, controlled breath.

items.heading: Bhramari Pranayama
details: Humming combined with controlled breathing can promote relaxation and calm the mind.

items.heading: Kapalabhati
details: Provides controlled respiratory activity; claims of literal physical "detoxification" are not established.

items.heading: Yoga Nidra
details: A structured relaxation practice that can reduce perceived stress and promote deep rest.

items.heading: Dhyana / Meditation
details: Regular practice can improve attention and reduce perceived stress in some people.

items.heading: Japa / Mantra repetition
details: Repetitive chanting can focus attention and naturally help regulate the breath.

items.heading: Mauna / Silence practice
details: Reduced sensory and social stimulation during periods of silence can facilitate reflection and relaxation.

items.heading: Ringing temple bells before entering the sanctum
details: A struck bell produces a sustained, high-frequency vibration lasting several seconds.
This sound is believed to help clear the mind of distractions right before entering a place of worship.

items.heading: Circumambulation (Pradakshina) around a deity or tree
details: Walking clockwise around a sacred space is a slow, meditative form of movement, similar to walking meditation.
Around trees especially, it encouraged people to spend time near green, oxygen-rich spaces.
